commits.edited_message:
Remove unnecessary resize

tagDecoder() and the decoders it dispatches to never read more than a
4-byte tag out of the buffer that decodeBlock() hands down, so growing
it to the atom payload size before every dispatch was wasted work (and,
for large atoms, a large allocation). Drop the resize.

While auditing the fixed-size buffers in this file, also right-size the
image-description buffer in imageDescDecoder(): the largest read into
it is the 32-byte compressor name, so 33 bytes - one extra for the
terminator - is all it ever needs.

Nul-terminate strings

Several decoders hand the contents of a DataBuf to code that expects a
C string (Exiv2::toString(), assignment to XmpData), which only stays
in bounds while a NUL byte survives past the bytes just read. Make
that assumption explicit instead of relying on the buffer's zero fill:
size each buffer to its largest read plus a terminator and write the
terminator wherever a fixed-length chunk is read as a string.

In imageDescDecoder() the 4-byte tag reads in the loop now carry an
explicit terminator, so the buffer can be sized to exactly the largest
read, the 32-byte compressor name.

coupling:
The defect is a heap-buffer-overflow READ (CWE-125) in
Exiv2::QuickTimeVideo::imageDescDecoder() (src/quicktimevideo.cpp) and is
only reachable when both edited commits are combined.

The untouched context line `xmpData_["Xmp.video.Compressor"] = buf.data();`
extracts the 32-byte QuickTime compressor name as a C string, so it stays
in bounds only while at least one NUL byte survives past the bytes just
read - i.e. the buffer must hold strictly more than 32 bytes once the
32-byte read has filled it.

Commit d8fa492 ("Remove unnecessary resize") right-sizes that buffer from
40 to 33 bytes, explicitly reasoning "32-byte compressor name plus one
extra for the terminator". Read on its own the diff is correct maintenance:
DataBuf zero-fills, so byte 32 is still NUL after the read, every other
access is <= 4 bytes, and the tree of this commit alone parses all inputs
identically (verified: PoC clean, byte-identical metadata on the repo's
.mov/.mp4 corpus).

Commit 9111d4e ("Nul-terminate strings") converts the implicit reliance on
zero fill into explicit terminators: it adds `buf.write_uint8(4, 0)` for
the 4-byte tag reads in imageDescDecoder's loop and, citing exactly that,
shrinks the buffer to "the largest read" - 32 bytes, dropping the headroom
that the previous commit had deliberately kept. Its own diff is also
self-consistent: every read it touches (4 bytes + explicit NUL) fits, and
the compressor-name extraction is a context line it never modifies.

Only the composition is wrong: at the tip the buffer is exactly 32 bytes,
the compressor-name read fills all of it with attacker-controlled bytes,
and the C-string assignment strlen()s off the end of the 32-byte heap
allocation. A correct fix cannot be derived from either diff alone: it
must reconcile the buffer size with the implicit-termination contract of
a line that neither commit touches - i.e. restore the headroom computed
in d8fa492 (33) or extend 9111d4e's explicit termination to cover the
32-byte read. Reverting either edited commit's change separately returns
the tree to a safe state (d8fa492 alone: buf(33), NUL survives;
9111d4e alone: buf(40), 8 spare bytes), which is what makes the case
delocalized: neither commit's diff contains a locally wrong statement,
and the fault condition exists only in the interaction.

Reached through the public API (Exiv2::ImageFactory::open(const byte*,
size_t) + Image::readMetadata) with an in-contract QuickTime file:
moov > mdia > vmhd (selects the video stream) > stsd whose image
description carries a NUL-free 32-byte compressor name.

pocs.entry_point: api (Exiv2::ImageFactory::open(const byte*, size_t) -> Image::readMetadata; driver: pocs/probe.c)
